modes.name: unrequested_narration_and_padding
modes.definition: The reply contains content the user did not ask for: a running commentary on what the agent is about to look up, a restated summary of facts already given, or extra policy detail beyond the question.
modes.boundary: Not commits_before_verification: this is about volume and commentary, not about asserting an outcome too early. A concise reply that states one fact the user asked for is a pass even if it also cites a policy id.
modes.requirement: SPEC gap: the system prompt currently REQUIRES narration before every tool call ('You MUST explain your reasoning in plain text before every tool call'), so the agent is complying. Fix the specification and prompt rather than evaluating against it. Related: RESP-5.

modes.name: scope_handling_overreach

modes.boundary: Naming its own capabilities, pointing at Cartwheel account settings, or escalating where the specification requires it (ESC-2) is NOT this failure. The line is an outward pointer. Refined 2026-09-23 after support-0143 ('check that marketplace's own seller support') was rejected as a close negative; it is a positive.

modes.name: commits_before_verification
modes.definition: The reply states an outcome (refund approved, order cancellable, return allowed) before the tool result or policy lookup that determines it has come back.
modes.boundary: Not unrequested_narration_and_padding: saying 'let me check' is padding; saying 'you are eligible' before the check is this mode. Verification test, set by the reviewer's depth-search decisions (2026-09-23): reading a record's own state (order status) from any lookup counts as verification, so support-0052 ('it hasn't shipped yet, so I can cancel it now' after find_order) is a pass; asserting refund or return eligibility requires check_return_eligibility, because eligibility depends on the store's window and the stored refund_eligible flag can be stale (it disagrees with the eligibility function on damaged order 8001), so support-0086 is a fail.

modes.name: ambiguity_resolved_by_guess
modes.definition: When more than one record matches what the user described, or the described quantity or item does not match the record found, the agent picks one and proceeds instead of asking which one.
modes.boundary: Not acts_without_authorization_check: the caller may see the records; the fault is choosing among them silently.

modes.name: exposes_internal_data_defect
modes.definition: The reply shows the user a broken or internal value (a negative price, contradictory dates, a bare store id) instead of reporting that the record is inconsistent and escalating.
modes.boundary: Not ambiguity_resolved_by_guess: the record is defective rather than ambiguous. Naming the defect and escalating without quoting the broken value is a pass.

modes.name: repeats_work_across_turns
modes.definition: On a later turn the agent redoes lookups or restates conclusions already established earlier in the same conversation, or ignores a correction the user made in an earlier turn.

retired_modes.name: acts_without_authorization_check
retired_modes.definition: The agent promises to open, or shows the content of, an order or store record before a tool result has confirmed the caller is authorized to see it.
retired_modes.boundary: Not a permission_denied trace: the tool layer refusing is correct behaviour. This mode is about what the reply asserts before that confirmation exists.
retired_modes.retired_reason: Authorization is enforced in the tool layer, not by the reply. agent/agent.py get_order_logic calls can_view_order(ctx, ...) and returns permission_denied when the caller is not entitled to the record (agent/auth.py:48); find_order derives its scope from the auth context (shopper -> own orders, merchant -> own store, all orders only for support). A successful tool result is therefore evidence that access was authorized, so a reply that reports it cannot be an authorization failure. The originating notes assumed the check was missing because it was not visible in the conversation. Two of them also misread their traces: support-0009's find_order results were already scoped to that shopper, and in support-0006 the merchant does own order 8003 (its *product* belongs to another store, which is the dq-order-store-mismatch defect).

agentdebug_comparison.observation: Two of our modes have no equivalent in the published taxonomy at all. AgentErrorTaxonomy classifies causes of task failure; this taxonomy also covers replies that complete the task but are wrong for a customer, which is the product requirement Cartwheel is judged on.
